宿主工具调用 deja CLI；Web 端单独走异步 DSH 历史搜索，自动召回在 prompt 组装时查询并返回本机历史。
抽读 extensions/dsh 的包、挂载、CLI 参数、自动上下文和网页路由。独立 deja 索引、核心 hook 新实现及真实宿主鉴权未核查。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) CLI 包装本身是小增量，网页过滤和会话归一化连接搜索结果与原宿主；[Q02](#research-q02) 独立控制自动路径有迁移价值，依赖 CLI 和宿主路由。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 减少在会话、终端和旧助手间的搬运，交付仍是可核实的历史原文；[Q03](#research-q03) 有机会覆盖不熟悉 CLI 的用户，检索与审查总成本未测。

      "content": "# dsh-deja

English | [中文](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/blob/main/extensions/dsh/docs/zh.md)

[![#1 Go Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/trendshift/repositories/83640/daily?language=Go)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/83640) [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/vshulcz/deja-vu?style=flat&label=Stars)](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/stargazers)

Part of **[deja-vu](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu)** (**97.2% R@5** on LongMemEval-S · **13.6 s** to index 19,195 sessions · **half the tokens** of agentmemory) · [Full documentation](../../README.md) · [Website & live search](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/) · [Browser demo](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/view/) · **[★ Star deja-vu on GitHub](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu)**

DeepSeek Harness can already search its own sessions — that is what the built-in
`session-query` subsystem does. This plugin answers the other question: what you
did in the *other* agents on this machine.

deja indexes the session files that forty-two other coding agents — Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor, opencode, Antigravity, Grok Build, Kimi, Cline and Zed among
them — already write to disk. Nothing has to have been recorded ahead of time: the history is already
there, including the months before deja was installed. If you moved to dsh last
week, everything you did before last week is still reachable from inside it.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-deja
```

From the repository instead of npm — the root manifest re-exports this
directory, so either form works:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:vshulcz/deja-vu#path:extensions/dsh
```

The plugin runs the `deja` binary. It is pulled in as a dependency, so npm
installs it with the plugin; a `deja` already on `PATH` is used as-is, and
`DEJA_BIN` overrides both.

If you have the CLI, `deja install --auto` wires dsh **and every other coding agent on this machine** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, Kimi, Cline, Zed and more) in one step — it adds deja's MCP server and a `/deja` command to your profile — and that is the shorter path:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/main/install.sh | sh
deja install --auto
```

Or with Homebrew: `brew install deja-vu && deja install --auto` · Try without installing: `npx @vshulcz/deja-vu sources`.
Having both is fine: this plugin looks for what the installer wrote in
`$DSH_HOME/plugins/deja/` and contributes only what is missing, so the tools and
the command are never registered twice.

## What it adds

Six tools the model can call:

| Tool | Answers |
|---|---|
| `deja_recall` | Sessions matching an error string, function name, file path or flag. |
| `deja_session` | The full digest of one past session, when the reasoning behind it matters. |
| `deja_blame` | The sessions that discussed a file, before you edit or delete it. |
| `deja_fix` | What this machine ran after that same error before. |
| `deja_how` | The real invocation for a build, test or deploy, from what ran here. |
| `deja_remember` | Stores one settled decision for later recall. |

One command: `/deja <what to look for>`.

And, unless you turn it off, automatic recall: once per session the plugin adds
what past sessions settled in this project, and before each step it asks deja
whether this machine's history answers the prompt and adds the answer to the
runtime context. Silence is the common case — it speaks only when there is
something to say.

The same recall also wires what `deja install dsh-auto` wires: after a read,
edit or write the model gets what past sessions said about that file, after a
command that failed it gets what this machine ran after the same error before,
a compaction keeps what the session was in the middle of, and a session that
ends drops its live stamp.

In `dsh web` you also see the lines deja prints for the person in Claude Code:
the receipt naming the agent a prompt's answer came from, and
at session start what was recalled, the first-build note and the weekly note.
They sit in a small panel above the input until the next prompt, or until you
close it. The model gets exactly what it got before; these lines never reach
it. tui, headless and sdk profiles have no page, so nothing changes there:
the notes still come with the reply to `/deja`. A line that waits more than
ten minutes for the page is dropped. `deja install dsh-auto` writes the same
panel from these files; with both installed you get one panel.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: deja
      name: dsh-deja
      config:
        autoRecall: false   # keep tools, /deja and manual search
```

## Search controls

Open **Settings → Deja** for three switches, all enabled by default and grouped
in two sections.

**In-conversation search**

- **Mod+F in conversations** writes a real `/deja` command into the message
  input — `/deja --session <bare session UUID> -- <your draft>` — and focuses
  it. Sending it runs deja against that one conversation, so the search
  actually happens instead of arriving as an ordinary message; reference
  chips in the draft are kept and move with the prefix. The shortcut does not
  send the draft; you send it when you choose. A draft that already starts
  with another command is left untouched. The default is **Mod+F** — in this
  document `Mod` means `Ctrl` on Windows/Linux and `Cmd` on macOS, and the
  defaults below are written in the registry's own `primary` form, which the
  framework expands per platform. In a browser the default is **Mod+Alt+F**
  (on macOS, **Cmd+Option+F**), because DSH reserves the browser's ordinary
  Find shortcut.

**Deja full-text search** (two switches)

- **Mod+Shift+K opens Deja full-text search** is the direct cross-session
  shortcut. It opens DSH's sidebar search and starts it in Deja full-text mode
  instead of the title search. The magnifying glass returns the native search
  for that opening. DSH's own **Mod+K** is left untouched: the shortcut
  registry rejects a second binding for the same key, so Deja uses
  **Mod+Shift+K** (**Cmd+Shift+K** on macOS), the same default on desktop and in
  a browser. Turn the switch off to restore the official behaviour completely.
- **Deja search in the sidebar** controls the magnifying-glass path. It adds a
  full-text mode to sidebar search: open sidebar search, then click its
  magnifying glass again to switch to Deja. Enter a query to search the local
  index of **DSH conversations only**, see up to 20 hits with matching
  snippets, and click a hit to open its session. Click the magnifying glass
  again to return to regular sidebar results. If more matches exist, narrow the
  query. Missing Deja, failed searches and sessions that cannot be opened are
  shown as errors.

**Linux browsers** get no default binding for either shortcut: the browser
service admits only `Mod+/`, `Mod+Shift+,` and `Mod+Shift+.`. `Mod+/` already
belongs to DSH's own `shortcuts.open` (the keyboard settings), so apart from the
other two (`Mod+Shift+,` and `Mod+Shift+.`) every combination is rejected.
Record one of those two in the settings below.

These preferences are saved separately in this browser/profile's local storage;
changing one does not change the other, and they do not sync between browsers
or devices. Manual search remains available with `autoRecall: false`.

### Customizing the shortcuts

Open **Settings → Deja → Customize shortcuts** to change the actual key
combinations. Three rows show the current binding for conversation search,
Deja cross-session search, and DSH's sidebar opener (`session.search`). Click
**Change shortcut**, press and release the desired combination, and it saves
immediately. **Restore default** restores that command's default; **Remove**
unbinds it. Escape or moving focus away cancels recording. Conflicts and save

remain subject to DSH's validation. Older DSH versions without the editing

tools and command can coexist with the package.

## How it is wired

Recall arrives through `ctx.systemPrompt.context`, evaluated on every assembly.
The obvious alternative — a middleware on `agent/pre-step` that splices a
message into the step — loads fine, completes the turn, and never reaches the
model: a later listener in that waterfall rebuilds its answer from the payload
and the added message is dropped with nothing reported. This was settled by
reading the requests dsh 0.1.1-rc.2 actually sent.

The person's lines take one deja call with the recall, not two: where dsh
serves the page, the plugin asks for the hook's JSON reply, hands `additionalContext` to the model and keeps
`systemMessage` on the host until the page asks for it at `/api/deja-notes`,
behind dsh's own login. Anywhere else it keeps asking for `--plain`, because
deja marks a note shown when it prints it. The browser half is `client.js`,
plain JS in dsh's module wrapper, so the package has no build step.

Manual sidebar search uses `GET /api/deja-search` on the same authenticated DSH
API mount. It runs an asynchronous, shell-free
`deja search --harness deepseek --json --limit 20 -- <query>` call, bounded to
20 seconds and 2 MiB of output. Empty queries launch no process; queries longer
than 500 characters are rejected. The route returns compact session metadata
and snippets rather than complete transcripts.

DSH currently exposes no sidebar-search provider API. The browser adapter stays
inside the `data-slot="sidebar.workspaces"` anchor and finds the semantic
`aria-expanded` search button and the `_listArea` CSS class suffix. This markup
was inspected in DSH **0.2.1-rc.5**. If those elements are absent in an older or
changed layout, the adapter leaves the regular sidebar alone. These internal
markup dependencies may need updating for future DSH versions.

## Testing the search controls

Run `node --test extensions/dsh/test/*.test.js` from the repository root for the
synthetic host, preferences, shortcut and composition tests. For the DOM/React
adapter check, serve the repository with a static HTTP server and open
`extensions/dsh/test/search-browser.html`. That optional fixture loads React

local index. A passing report covers mode switching, session opening, host
errors, empty queries, disabling the feature and cleanup.

## What it does not do

No LLM, no embeddings. The index is a local BM25 store over files
that already exist, so a query answers in about a millisecond, with no network
path unless you ask for one. Secrets are redacted at index time.

## Search it yourself

`deja` with no arguments opens a terminal search across every agent's history — starting with
the sessions behind your uncommitted changes, then recent work in the current project.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/main/assets/tui.gif" width="720" alt="Typing a search in the deja screen, reading the session it found, and continuing that session in another agent"></p>

- **Navigate:** `↑↓` picks a session, `↵` opens at the match, `/` searches inside a session, `]` `[` jump between turns, `^s` toggles date/relevance sort (`deja search --sort date`).
- **Filter:** by agent (`codex:`), time (`today`, `yesterday`, `week`, `month`), or project (`in:<project>`).
- **Resume or hand off:** `r` reopens the session in its native agent; `o` continues it in another agent with its goal, decisions and open work.
- **Recover deleted chats:** `tab` switches between this project, all projects, and **Deleted** (sessions an agent purged that deja still holds); `R` restores one, `D` deletes (`deja delete <id>`), `?` lists all keys.

Prefer a browser? `deja view` exports the store — sessions, the recall audit trail, and promoted notes — into one local HTML file ([try the live demo](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/view/)). With `DEJA_TUI=0` (or `deja brief`), `deja` prints a plain-text summary.

## Highlights

- **Starts full on day one.** Months of existing transcripts across all [forty-three agents](#supported-harnesses) are searchable immediately — fix a bug in Codex and Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode recalls it.
- **Survives `/compact` and context resets.** Over 43 measured compactions, summaries kept 77% of decisions and 0.2% of commands; deja hands back the exact commands, errors, and decisions ([how](docs/compaction.md)).
- **Cross-agent handoff (`deja handoff`).** Hit a rate limit or get stuck in Claude Code? Hand the active session's goal, decisions, touched files, and open work straight into Codex, Cursor, or OpenCode.
- **Undo overwritten code (`deja restore` & `deja blame`).** Indexes opened files, commands with exit codes, and exact `Edit` spans so `deja restore <path>` recovers code an agent clobbered even before `git commit` (`deja blame <file>:<line>`).
- **Automatic recall via hooks & MCP.** Surfaces prior sessions at session start, before a file edit or command runs, and when a command fails.
- **Tracks decision lifecycle & staleness.** `deja promote <id> --state rejected` marks a reverted approach so later hits warn why it was dropped (`--state accepted` takes the mark back), and hits report when files touched by a session have changed since.
- **Travels with the repository.** `deja repo add` commits the decisions and dead ends you pick into `.deja/memory.jsonl`; a teammate's agent recalls them after a clone ([repo memory](#memory-in-the-repository)).
- **Incremental local index.** Append-only `records.bin` plus token buckets in `~/.cache/deja`, with per-file watermarks in `manifest.gob` so repeat passes only read changed files (~50 ms freshness check; 4% index footprint on a 5.7 GB / 358k-message corpus). Zero LLM calls, no cloud account, and automatic credential redaction at index time ([architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [privacy](#privacy)).

## Memory in the repository

Sync moves history between your own machines. To hand the people you work with the
few things your agents learned the hard way, put them in the repository:

```text
$ deja repo candidates
4cd7e7bb9c rejected Reverted the retry with jitter: it broke idempotency because the sender re-signs each attempt with a new delivery id.  (session s1, claude 2026-08-03)
$ deja repo add 4cd7e7bb9c
added 1 entry to .deja/memory.jsonl
nothing is committed: review with `git diff .deja/` and commit it like code
```

Candidates come from this project's history in every agent: promoted and remembered
notes, reversals reported in a session, and what sessions settled. Nothing is written
until you pick, every entry is redacted on the way in, and one that still matches a secret
rule is refused. The file is JSON lines sorted by a content hash, with a
`merge=union` attribute beside it, so parallel additions merge; deleting a line removes
an entry. After a clone, the entries come back at session start and in recall, in any agent
deja is wired into, marked as from the repository and framed as untrusted like the rest.
`{"activations":{"auto":{"repo":false}}}` in the trust policy keeps them out of the hooks.
[More](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/repo-memory.html).

## Privacy

Indexing and search are local. The network is used only by `deja update`, `deja sync ssh`,
the version check in `deja doctor`, `deja embed` against an endpoint you configure (and,
once it has built the semantic sidecar, each search, which sends the query to that
endpoint), and a once-a-day look at the latest release from an interactive command. That look sends no
session data; `DEJA_OFFLINE=1` turns it off, and so does `DEJA_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE` set to any
value, which also hides the note a new version prints on its first run.

Credentials are stripped as the index is built: cloud and provider keys, tokens and JWTs,
PEM blocks, passwords in URLs or stated in prose. Each becomes `[redacted:<kind>]` and the
text around it stays searchable. The source transcripts still hold them
([one machine had 84 in 42 sessions](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/credentials-in-transcripts.html)):
`deja secrets` names those sessions without printing a value, and `deja secrets --scrub`
rewrites the ones it can, keeping the original beside the file.

`deja forget` drops sessions and keeps them dropped across rebuilds. `~/.config/deja/exclude`
skips a project per line, or a whole store with `harness:opencode`. The
[security model](docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md) has the data flows and what redaction cannot catch.

## CLI

Bare `deja` in a terminal opens [the search screen](#search-it-yourself). With a query,
or any command below, it prints and exits:

```text
$ deja "jwt refresh token"
[claude] api        · Jul 8 · 8f31c0a9 — 2 matches
  login started failing after refresh token rotation; jwt kid mismatch in tests
  fixed by reloading jwks cache after rotateKey and adding a clock-skew test
[codex]  web        · Jul 1 · b77d91e2 — 1 match
  refresh token cookie needed SameSite=Lax in local callback flow
```

**Ask your history**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `deja <query>` | Search every history. Multi-word is AND and quoted phrases require contiguous text; a query with no exact match then tries word forms and close spellings, which is where a substring reaches its word (`code` finds `opencode`). `--sort date` lists the newest match first. |
| `deja` | In a terminal, the full-screen search above. `deja brief` prints the text summary instead: today's sessions, what deja served, recent work and a search to try. |
| `deja wip` | What the last session in this directory was doing: the task, what it settled, the files in flight, the last command and whether it failed — derived from the transcript, not from a note someone remembered to write. |
| `deja blame <path>[:line]` | Which sessions discussed a file, what was decided, and why. With a line: the commit that last changed it, and the session that wrote that line or the text the commit replaced. `--attribution` prints the line answer alone, as JSON with `--json`, and `--git-note` records it in `refs/notes/deja`. |
| `deja origin [rev\|range]` | Which session and user turn produced a commit or commit range, matched against recorded edit spans (`attributed`, `uncertain`, or `unknown`). |
| `deja review [rev\|range]` | Prior sessions and settled notes (`.deja/notes.jsonl` and personal notes) for the files changed in a working-tree diff, commit, or range. |
| `deja files <topic>` | The other direction: which files the work on a subject actually touched. |
| `deja how <tool>` | How this machine actually runs a thing, with the real flags, from what agents ran before. |
| `deja fix <error>` | What this machine ran after that same error before, when the error did not come back. Never a merge, a force push or a deletion. |
| `deja friction` | Errors that hit three or more separate sessions, with the harnesses named. |

When the first word of a bare query has at least four characters and is one
edit from a command name, deja names that command on stderr and then searches
as usual. `deja search <query>` skips the suggestion.

## Semantic recall (optional)

Point `deja embed` at a local Ollama, LM Studio or OpenAI-compatible endpoint with
`DEJA_EMBED_URL` and rephrased queries still hit. Without a reachable runtime, lexical
search and MCP recall continue unchanged. OpenAI Platform works with its standard key:

```sh
export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'
export DEJA_EMBED_URL='https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings'
export DEJA_EMBED_MODEL='text-embedding-3-small'
deja embed
```

<details>
<summary>Local runtimes, other endpoints, and what vectors cost</summary>

With no `DEJA_EMBED_URL` set, deja probes `localhost:11434` and `localhost:1234`,
so a machine already running Ollama or LM Studio is picked up without being asked.
`DEJA_EMBED_OFF=1`, or `DEJA_EMBED_URL=off`, turns that probe off — any other
configured `DEJA_EMBED_URL` still wins.

For another authenticated OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set `DEJA_EMBED_KEY` explicitly:

```sh
export DEJA_EMBED_URL='https://example.com/v1/embeddings'
export DEJA_EMBED_MODEL='embedding-model'
export DEJA_EMBED_KEY='...'
deja embed
```

`DEJA_EMBED_KEY` takes precedence. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is used automatically only for an
HTTPS `api.openai.com` URL; it is never implicitly sent to local or third-party endpoints.

Models trained with instruction prefixes, such as the multilingual E5 family, need them on
both sides. `DEJA_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX` goes in front of every search query and
`DEJA_EMBED_PASSAGE_PREFIX` in front of every indexed text; both are empty by default:

```sh
export DEJA_EMBED_MODEL='multilingual-e5-small'
export DEJA_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX='query: '
export DEJA_EMBED_PASSAGE_PREFIX='passage: '
deja embed
```

The passage prefix is part of the sidecar's model name, so changing it embeds everything
again, and search ignores vectors made with another model or prefix (it says so once).

The sidecar sits beside the index as `.vectors.bin`, not inside `index.db`. Float32 vectors
cost roughly 4 MB per 1k messages for a 1,024 dimension model. A remote endpoint receives
the redacted indexed text, truncated to about 2k characters, but never raw source files.
With Ollama or LM Studio, embedding stays local and needs no key.

</details>

## Proof

Millisecond lookups, and on LongMemEval-S 88.9% hit@1 (470-question cleaned set) and 88.2% hit@1 on all 500 questions;
on LoCoMo retrieval, 71.9% hit@1. On a task this machine had already solved, 58% fewer
tokens: eleven runs an arm, 53,558 against 126,222 with nothing wired, and 52,815 against
103,443 on a later build with the arms alternated. Both retrieval harnesses ship in this repo
and run on the public datasets in minutes: [benchmarks](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/benchmarks.html) ·
[what one task costs](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/day-zero.html).

The rest is measured by `deja bench`:

```sh
deja bench recall     # ranking floor: 100 queries, half Russian, CI fails if recall drops
deja bench context    # 30 seeded task chains plus five negative controls
deja bench block      # does the answer survive into what deja hands over
deja bench prompt     # what the per-prompt hook fires on, and what it fires on wrongly
deja bench ingest     # what an update costs: unchanged, a turn, a new transcript, a rename, a rewrite
deja bench read       # what it costs to read a database-backed store, and what one long value does to it
```

<details>
<summary>What the in-repo benches measure, and lookup cost on a real store</summary>

`bench block` asks the question the others cannot: with the right session in
hand, does the block carry what that session settled. Eight sessions discuss each
subject and one of them settles it, in the middle of its own transcript rather
than at the end — so the baseline arm, the newest turns of the top hit, scores
zero and an arm above zero had to choose.

| Arm | Carries the answer | Median tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `deja-block` (session-start block) | 1.00 | 665 |
| `deja-digest` (context digest) | 1.00 | 1656 |
| `newest-turn` (baseline) | 0.00 | 289 |
| `cold` | 0.00 | 0 |


The context experiment compares deja-recall against full-history, naive grep and cold
context. With the default seed:

| Arm | Median tokens | Median coverage | Negative-control tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| deja-recall | 1,096 | 1.00 | 0 |
| full-history | 80,547 | 1.00 | 78,145 |
| naive-grep | 273,238 | 1.00 | 0 |
| cold | 0 | 0.00 | 0 |

Same fact coverage as grepping the raw logs for about 250x fewer tokens, and about 70x
fewer than replaying the matched sessions in full, while injecting nothing on the chains
where no prior fact is relevant. The corpus generator and the relevance labels are
ordinary reviewed Go. Audit what "relevant" means before trusting any figure, ours
included.

Measured on a real store of 2,419 sessions and 179k messages, 1.9 GB of
transcripts:

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Lookup, in process | **0.7–0.8 ms** median (`deja bench recall`, 100 queries, half of them Russian), ~15 ms on the LongMemEval-S haystacks |
| `deja <query>`, end to end | ~0.2 s median on that store: process start, the freshness check over every store, ranking, printing |
| Freshness check alone | ~50 ms when nothing changed |
| Index size | 200 MB, ~10% of corpus |

The same store has since grown to 2,754 sessions, 358k messages and 5.7 GB.
A cold full build over it takes 71 s and writes a 232 MB index — 4% of the
corpus, because the share falls as transcripts repeat themselves — and the
end-to-end median is unchanged at 0.25 s. Since 0.23.2 records are compressed
from 256 bytes, which takes a 19k-session index from 277 to 185 MB.

The index is incremental. When a session file grows, only that file is re-read. When one is
rewritten, its new records are appended and the old ones zeroed in place. On a
40,000-session store a pass over 20 rewritten transcripts takes 1.7 s and peaks under 1 GB,
and a search for a word most sessions hold takes about a second.

</details>

## How it works

Local inverted index in `~/.cache/deja`: parse the JSONL and SQLite stores, redact
credentials, write an append-only `records.bin` plus token buckets, and track per-file state in
`manifest.gob` so repeat runs only ingest what changed. The MCP server, stats, share and
sync all read that one index. Details in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

<details>
<summary><b>Will it slow my agent down?</b></summary>

A recall is a lexical lookup against a local index:
0.7–0.8 ms median, and nothing waits on a model. A hook adds the process start and a
freshness check over your stores on top of that: about 0.2 s end to end on a 1.9 GB
store. On an index of 19k sessions the per-prompt hook takes 107 ms at the median,
and a recall through `deja mcp` 85 ms.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Where is Claude Code session history stored, and can I search it?</b></summary>

Under `~/.claude/projects`, one JSONL file per session; Codex keeps `~/.codex/sessions`, Cursor a
SQLite `state.vscdb`. deja reads them all in place: bare `deja` opens a screen to search
and read them, `deja search` does it from a script, `deja last` lists the recent
sessions of every agent, and `deja view` opens the whole history as one local page. Paths
for each agent: [where sessions are stored](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/where-sessions-are-stored.html).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>My Claude Code session history disappeared. Is it gone?</b></summary>

Claude Code deletes transcripts older than 30 days (`cleanupPeriodDays` in `~/.claude/settings.json`), and `claude --resume` lists
only what is left. A session deja indexed before the cleanup stays searchable after the
file is gone, and the weekly note at session start says how many it kept, with an id
`deja resume <id> --write-back` puts back. Details: [session files on disk](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/session-files-on-disk.html).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>What files live in ~/.config/deja, and what can I set in them?</b></summary>

Under `~/.config/deja` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deja`):

- **`policy.json`** (`DEJA_POLICY_FILE` moves it) — JSON object with four optional keys:
  - `"activations"`: per-surface origin rules for `"search"`, `"mcp"` and `"auto"` (hooks), keyed by `"local"`, `"imported"`, `"imported:<group>"` or `"*"` (`true`/`false`). `DEJA_AUTORECALL_LOCAL_ONLY=1` sets `activations.auto.imported` to `false`.
  - `"ignore"`: array of shell globs matched against session path and project to exclude from recall and `sync` (default `["*/.claude/jobs/*"]`).
  - `"auto_index"`: `false` stops automatic index updates on search, MCP recall and hooks (same as `DEJA_NO_AUTO_INDEX=1`).
  - `"search_only"`: `true` skips mining fixes, commands and co-occurrence, saving ~20% of build CPU (same as `DEJA_SEARCH_ONLY=1`).
- **`exclude`** — one project name or path pattern per line to skip at index time and `sync export`, or `harness:<name>` (e.g. `harness:opencode`) to skip a store (`DEJA_EXCLUDE_PROJECTS`, `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES`).
- **`projects`** — one `<path> = <name>` per line to group multiple checkouts or worktrees as one project.
- **`rules.md`** — standing instructions copied into each installed agent's global rules file by `deja rules sync`.
- **State files written by deja** — `peers.json` (`deja sync ssh`), `settled.json` (`deja friction --settle`), `tombstones` (`deja forget`), `wiring.json` and `bin/deja-hook` (`deja install`).

Hook recall mode is set by `DEJA_RECALL`: `safe` (default, 2 KB cap and up to 3 sessions from the current project at session start), `aggressive` (4 KB cap and up to 6 sessions across projects), or `off` (silences all hooks). The `DEJA_INDEX_*` switches and full configuration table are in the [commands guide](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/commands.html#configuration).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>One project is spread over several checkouts. Can recall treat them as one?</b></summary>

List the trees in `~/.config/deja/projects`, one `<path> = <name>` per line:

```text
~/work/monorepo = work
~/work/worktrees = work
```

Every directory under a listed path is then that project, for indexing, the hooks and recall alike; the longest matching path wins. Run `deja index --rebuild` to re-file existing transcripts under the new name. The exclude file still wins over project aliases.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How do I wipe everything?</b></summary>

```sh
deja uninstall --all
rm -rf ~/.cache/deja ~/.local/share/deja ~/.config/deja
```

The index is under `~/.cache/deja`, your `remember` and `promote` notes in
`~/.local/share/deja`, and the rules, exclude list, project aliases and hook launcher in
`~/.config/deja` (or under `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when set; on
Windows the notes are in `%AppData%\deja`).

</details>

      parsed.notes.forEach((n, i) => body.push(noteRow(n, "n" + i)));
      // Links stay in view: the docs, the tracker and the one-time sentence
      // share one small footer row rather than queueing behind "more".
      const footer = [
        ...parsed.links.map((l, i) => link(l.href, l.label, "a" + i)),
        ...parsed.linked.map((l, i) => h("span", { key: "s" + i, className: "deja-linked" }, link(l.href, l.text))),
      ];
      if (body.length === 0 && footer.length === 0) return null;
      const hidden = open ? 0 : Math.max(0, body.length - VISIBLE);
      if (hidden > 0) {
        footer.unshift(h("button", { key: "more", type: "button", className: "deja-more", onClick: () => setOpen(true) }, hidden + " more"));
      }
      return h(
        "div",
        { className: "deja-card", "data-deja-notes": "", role: "status" },
        h(
          "div",
          { className: "deja-head" },
          h("a", { className: "deja-name", href: "https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu", target: "_blank", rel: "noopener noreferrer" }, "deja-vu"),
          h("button", { type: "button", className: "deja-close", title: "Dismiss", "aria-label": "Dismiss deja-vu notes", onClick: onClose }, "×"),

    }

    function DejaNotes(props) {
      const sessionId = props && props.sessionId;
      const useSession = props && typeof props.useSession === "function" ? props.useSession : null;
      const running = useSession ? useSession((s) => Boolean(s && s.running)) : null;
      const [lines, setLines] = React.useState([]);

      // A new session or a new turn starts clean: a receipt answers the prompt
      // it came with, and left standing under the next one it would name the
      // wrong question. The session check stands on its own, because dsh may
      // keep this component and hand it another idle session.
      React.useEffect(() => {
        setLines([]);
      }, [sessionId]);
      React.useEffect(() => {
        if (running === true) setLines([]);
      }, [running]);

      React.useEffect(() => {
        if (!sessionId) return undefined;
        let alive = true;
        const ask = () =>
          pull(sessionId).then((notes) => {
            if (alive && notes.length > 0) setLines((held) => [...held, ...notes].slice(-8));
          });
        ask();
        // The recall runs while the turn's context is assembled, which may be
        // a moment after the page sees the turn start; the end of the turn
        // asks again. A host without useSession gets a slow poll instead.
        const timers = [];
        if (running === true) timers.push(setTimeout(ask, 800), setTimeout(ask, 2500));
        const poll = running === null ? setInterval(ask, 4000) : null;
        return () => {
          alive = false;
          timers.forEach(clearTimeout);
          if (poll) clearInterval(poll);
        };
      }, [sessionId, running]);

      if (lines.length === 0) return null;
      return h(Card, { lines, onClose: () => setLines([]) });
    }

    // Preferences belong to this browser/profile, like DSH's keybindings.
    const SEARCH_PREFS = "dsh.deja.search.v1";
    function preferences(storage) {
      let value = { conversation: true, sidebar: true, opensDeja: true };
      try {
        const saved = JSON.parse(storage.getItem(SEARCH_PREFS));
        for (const key of Object.keys(value)) if (typeof saved?.[key] === "boolean") value[key] = saved[key];
      } catch {}
      const listeners = new Set();
      // Mod+Shift+K opens DSH's sidebar search and switches it to Deja's
      // full-text mode via requestOpen(); native Mod+K is untouched.
      let pendingOpen = false;
      const openListeners = new Set();
      return {
        requestOpen() {
          if (!value.sidebar || !value.opensDeja) return;
          pendingOpen = true;
          for (const fn of openListeners) fn();
        },
        onOpen(fn) {
          openListeners.add(fn);
          if (pendingOpen) fn();
          return () => openListeners.delete(fn);
        },
        getSnapshot: () => value,
        subscribe(fn) { listeners.add(fn); return () => listeners.delete(fn); },
        set(key, enabled) {
          if (!(key in value)) return;
          value = { ...value, [key]: Boolean(enabled) };
          try { storage.setItem(SEARCH_PREFS, JSON.stringify(value)); } catch {}
          for (const fn of listeners) fn();
        },
        // When Deja owns the Mod+Shift+K gesture, the search it opens becomes
        // Deja's. The magnifier click and re-open interactions reset the
        // flag, so the native view stays reachable.
        claimOpen() {
          if (!value.opensDeja || !value.sidebar) return false;
          pendingOpen = true;
          return true;
        },
        releaseOpen() {
          const wasPending = pendingOpen;
          pendingOpen = false;
          return wasPending;
        },
      };
    }

    function usePreferences(prefs) {
      const [value, setValue] = React.useState(prefs.getSnapshot);
      React.useEffect(() => prefs.subscribe(() => setValue(prefs.getSnapshot())), [prefs]);
      return value;
    }

    // The sidebar mode and its shortcut query the host route the package's
    // index.js installs. `deja install dsh-auto` loads this same file as the
    // deja-notes card without that route; a 404 there means the search would
    // only ever fail, so the whole feature stands down instead of showing a
    // dead entry. The empty query is the route's own launch-nothing path, so
    // the probe never starts a deja search.
    const routeKey = Symbol.for("dsh-deja.search-route");
    function searchRoute() {
      if (window[routeKey]) return window[routeKey];
      let status = "unknown", started = false, decided = false, version = "";
      const listeners = new Set();
      const publish = (next, nextVersion) => {
        if (typeof nextVersion === "string") version = nextVersion;
        if (status === next) return;
        status = next;
        for (const fn of [...listeners]) fn();
      };
      const store = window[routeKey] = {
        getSnapshot: () => status,
        getVersion: () => version,
        subscribe(fn) { listeners.add(fn); return () => listeners.delete(fn); },
        // A host that knows its own state (a test, or a mount that shipped
        // with the route) can declare it; declaring stops the probe from
        // second-guessing it later.
        set(next, nextVersion) { decided = true; publish(next, nextVersion); return store; },
        probe(send = typeof fetch === "function" ? fetch : null) {
          if (started || decided) return store;
          started = true;
          if (!send) { publish("absent"); return store; }
          Promise.resolve()
            .then(() => send("api/deja-search?probe=1", {
              credentials: "same-origin", cache: "no-store", headers: { accept: "application/json" },
            }))
            .then(async (response) => {
              if (decided) return;
              // Fetch Response has `ok`; minimal test doubles only carry
              // `status`. Accept either, but never a 4xx/5xx or a failed
              // request as evidence of a working route.
              const ok = response && (response.ok === true ||
                (response.ok === undefined && typeof response.status === "number" &&
                  response.status >= 200 && response.status < 300));
              if (!ok) { publish("absent"); return; }
              // Only the route's own probe payload proves a working endpoint.
              // A 500, an SPA HTML fallback, or a proxy error must not enable
              // a sidebar toggle that has nothing behind it.
              try {
                const body = response.json ? await response.json() : null;
                if (decided) return;
                if (body && body.ok === true && body.plugin === "dsh-deja") {
                  publish("present", String(body.version || ""));
                } else {
                  publish("absent");
                }
              } catch { if (!decided) publish("absent"); }
            }, () => { if (!decided) publish("absent"); });
          return store;
        },
      };
      return store;
    }

    function useSearchRoute(route) {
      const [status, setStatus] = React.useState(route.getSnapshot);
      React.useEffect(() => {
        const update = () => setStatus(route.getSnapshot());
        const off = route.subscribe(update);
        // Read once on subscribe: a store handed in later may already answer.
        update();
        return off;
      }, [route]);
      return status;
    }

    // Mod+F writes a real `/deja` command, so the search runs when the
    // person sends it — a plain "deja search" sentence would only be a message
    // to the model. The draft keeps its reference chips by shifting every
    // occurrence past the prefix; the shape is DSH's own draft snapshot.
    const SESSION_COMMAND = "/deja";
    function bareSession(id) {
      const bare = String(id || "").replace(/^session-/, "");
      return /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/.test(bare) ? bare : "";
    }
    function sessionDraft(id, projection) {
      const bare = bareSession(id);
      if (!bare) return null;
      const prefix = SESSION_COMMAND + " --session " + bare + " -- ";
      const text = typeof projection?.clipboardText === "string" ? projection.clipboardText : "";
      const command = { token: SESSION_COMMAND };
      const occurrences = Array.isArray(projection?.occurrences) ? projection.occurrences : [];
      // A different command chip leads this draft; rewriting it would replace
      // the command the person typed, so leave their draft as it is.
      if (projection?.command && !text.startsWith(prefix)) return null;
      // Repeated Mod+F focuses the same draft instead of nesting prefixes.
      const shift = text.startsWith(prefix) ? 0 : prefix.length;
      return {
        text: shift ? prefix + text : text,
        command,
        references: occurrences.map((row) => ({
          source: String(row.source || ""),
          ref: String(row.ref || ""),
          label: String(row.label || ""),
          offset: Number(row.offset) + shift,
          length: Number(row.length),
          clipboardText: String(row.clipboardText || ""),
          ...(row.appearance ? { appearance: row.appearance } : {}),
          ...(row.invalid ? { invalid: true } : {}),
        })),
      };
    }

    function installFind(ctx, prefs) {
      return ctx.shortcuts.register({
        id: "deja.search-session",
        label: () => "Deja: search this conversation",
        aliases: ["deja", "find in conversation"],
        defaults: Object.fromEntries([
          ...["windows", "macos", "linux"].map((os) => ["desktop:" + os, { code: "KeyF", modifiers: ["primary"] }]),
          // The browser service admits only a short allowlist on web:linux
          // (primary+Slash, primary+shift+Comma, primary+shift+Period) or
          // three or more modifiers. Any other combination makes register()
          // throw, which would leave the command unregistered everywhere.
          // web:linux therefore declares no default; an omitted profile is
          // unbound, and the person there records their own combination.
          ...["windows", "macos"].map((os) => ["web:" + os, { code: "KeyF", modifiers: ["primary", "alt"] }]),
        ]),
        regions: ["page", "editable"],
        modals: [],
        resolve(context) {
          if (!prefs.getSnapshot().conversation || context.modal != null || context.region === "terminal") return { status: "pass" };
          const id = ctx.uiSession.current.getSnapshot().key;
          const binding = id && ctx.sessions.binding(id);
          if (!binding || !bareSession(id)) return { status: "pass" };
          return { status: "handled", run() {
            // Resolve again: navigation can change between key resolution and execution.
            const current = ctx.uiSession.current.getSnapshot().key;
            const active = current && ctx.sessions.binding(current);
            if (!active) return;
            const input = ctx.conversation.input.for(active.ctx);
            const draft = sessionDraft(current, input.projection);
            if (!draft) return;
            input.actions.setDraft(draft);
            input.actions.persistDraft();
            input.focus();
          } };
        },
      });
    }

    // All edits go through DSH so native menu bindings, conflict checks and
    // per-platform persistence stay in sync with the built-in shortcut editor.
    function bindingEditor(shortcuts, id, changed) {
      let alive = true, recording = false, busy = false, starting = false, candidate = null, revision;
      let generation = 0;
      let protection = Promise.resolve();
      const emit = (message = "") => { if (alive) changed({ recording, busy, starting, message }); };
      const stop = () => {
        generation++;
        recording = false;
        candidate = null;
        // Serialize stop after start, including disposal during bridge startup.
        protection = protection.catch(() => {}).then(() => shortcuts.recording(false));
        protection.catch(() => {});
      };
      const save = async (operation) => {
        if (!alive || busy) return;
        busy = true;
        stop();
        emit();
        try {
          await protection;
          if (!alive) return;
          const result = await shortcuts.edit(operation, revision);
          emit(result.status === "saved" ? "Saved" : "Save failed: " + result.status + ". Record again and retry.");
        } catch (error) { emit("Save failed: " + error.message); }
        finally { busy = false; if (alive) changed({ recording, busy, message: null }); }
      };
      return {
        async start() {
          if (!alive || busy || recording) return;
          if (shortcuts.config.getSnapshot().status !== "ready") { emit("Shortcut settings are not ready yet."); return; }
          revision = shortcuts.config.getSnapshot().revision;
          busy = true; starting = true;
          const attempt = ++generation;
          emit();
          protection = protection.catch(() => {}).then(() => shortcuts.recording(true));
          try { await protection; if (alive && attempt === generation) { recording = true; emit("Press a combination, then release to save; Esc cancels."); } }
          catch { stop(); emit("Could not enable recording protection. Try again."); }
          finally { busy = false; starting = false; if (alive) changed({ recording, busy, starting, message: null }); }
        },
        keydown(event) {
          if (!recording) return;
          event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation();
          if (event.code === "Escape") { stop(); emit("Cancelled"); return; }
          if (event.isComposing || event.key === "Dead" || event.getModifierState?.("AltGraph")) {
            stop(); emit("Cannot record during input-method composition or AltGraph. Try again."); return;
          }
          if (event.repeat || /^(Control|Alt|Shift|Meta)(Left|Right)$/.test(event.code)) return;
          if (event.code === "Tab" && !event.ctrlKey && !event.altKey && !event.metaKey) { stop(); emit("Cancelled"); return; }
          if (candidate) { candidate = null; stop(); emit("Record one combination at a time."); return; }
          try {
            const binding = { code: event.code, modifiers: [
              event.ctrlKey && "control", event.altKey && "alt", event.shiftKey && "shift", event.metaKey && "meta",
            ].filter(Boolean) };
            const description = shortcuts.describeBinding(binding);
            const conflicts = description.conflicts.filter((other) => other !== id);
            if (description.issue || conflicts.length) {
              const catalog = shortcuts.catalog.getSnapshot();
              const labels = conflicts.map((other) => catalog.find((row) => row.id === other)?.label || other);
              stop(); emit(conflicts.length ? "Shortcut conflict: " + labels.join(", ") : "Combination unavailable: " + description.issue);
              return;
            }
            candidate = description.binding;
            emit(description.keys.join(" ") + " — release to save");
          } catch { stop(); emit("This combination is not supported."); }
        },
        keyup(event) {
          if (!recording) return;
          event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation();
          const modifier = /^(Control|Alt|Shift|Meta)(Left|Right)$/.exec(event.code)?.[1]?.toLowerCase();
          if (candidate && (event.code === candidate.code || candidate.modifiers.includes(modifier))) {
            return save({ type: "set", id, binding: candidate });
          }
        },
        cancel() { if (recording || starting) { stop(); emit("Cancelled"); } },
        reset() {
          revision = shortcuts.config.getSnapshot().revision;
          return save({ type: "reset", id });
        },
        clear() {
          revision = shortcuts.config.getSnapshot().revision;
          return save({ type: "set", id, binding: null });
        },
        activate() { alive = true; },
        dispose() { alive = false; if (recording || busy) stop(); },
      };
    }

    function useShortcutStore(store) {
      const [value, setValue] = React.useState(() => store.getSnapshot());
      React.useEffect(() => {
        const update = () => setValue(store.getSnapshot());
        const dispose = store.subscribe(update);
        update();
        return dispose;
      }, [store]);
      return value;
    }

    function ShortcutBinding({ shortcuts, id, title }) {
      const catalog = useShortcutStore(shortcuts.catalog);
      const config = useShortcutStore(shortcuts.config);
      const [state, setState] = React.useState({ recording: false, busy: false, message: "" });
      const editor = React.useMemo(() => bindingEditor(shortcuts, id, (next) => setState((old) => ({
        ...next, message: next.message === null ? old.message : next.message,
      }))), [shortcuts, id]);

        editor.activate();
        const cancel = () => editor.cancel();
        window.addEventListener("blur", cancel);
        document.addEventListener("compositionstart", cancel, true);
        return () => {
          window.removeEventListener("blur", cancel);
          document.removeEventListener("compositionstart", cancel, true);
          editor.dispose();
        };

      const recorder = React.useRef(null);
      React.useEffect(() => {
        if (!state.recording) return;
        recorder.current?.focus();
        const down = (event) => { if (document.activeElement === recorder.current) editor.keydown(event); };
        const up = (event) => { if (document.activeElement === recorder.current) editor.keyup(event); };
        document.addEventListener("keydown", down, true);
        document.addEventListener("keyup", up, true);
        return () => {
          document.removeEventListener("keydown", down, true);
          document.removeEventListener("keyup", up, true);
        };

      const disabled = !row || config.status !== "ready" || state.busy;
      return h("div", { className: "deja-setting deja-keybinding" },
        h("div", null, h("strong", null, title),
          h("div", { className: "deja-setting-hint" }, row?.keys?.join(" ") || "Not bound")),
        h("button", { type: "button", ref: recorder, disabled: !row || config.status !== "ready" || (state.busy && !state.starting), "aria-label": "Change the " + title + " shortcut",
          onClick: () => editor.start(), onBlur: () => editor.cancel(),
        }, state.recording ? "Press a combination…" : "Change shortcut"),
        h("button", { type: "button", disabled: disabled || state.recording, onClick: () => editor.reset() }, "Restore default"),
        h("button", { type: "button", disabled: disabled || state.recording, onClick: () => editor.clear() }, "Remove"),
        h("span", { role: "status", className: "deja-setting-hint" }, state.message),
      );
    }

    // What an install needs to say, and how the page offers it: the sidebar
    // mode cannot work without the package's route, so the settings page names
    // the endpoint and its version, and hands over the command when it is
    // missing instead of leaving a dead switch.
    const INSTALL_COMMAND = "dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-deja";

    async function copyText(text) {
      try {
        if (navigator?.clipboard?.writeText) { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text); return true; }
      } catch {}
      try {
        const area = document.createElement("textarea");
        area.value = text;
        area.setAttribute("readonly", "");
        area.style.position = "fixed";
        area.style.opacity = "0";
        document.body.appendChild(area);
        area.select();
        const copied = document.execCommand("copy");
        area.remove();
        return copied;
      } catch { return false; }
    }

    function useRouteVersion(route) {
      const [version, setVersion] = React.useState(() => route.getVersion ? route.getVersion() : "");
      React.useEffect(() => {
        const update = () => setVersion(route.getVersion ? route.getVersion() : "");
        const off = route.subscribe(update);
        update();
        return off;
      }, [route]);
      return version;
    }

    function EndpointStatus({ route }) {
      const status = useSearchRoute(route);
      const version = useRouteVersion(route);
      const [copied, setCopied] = React.useState(false);

        h("h3", null, "Search endpoint"),
        h("p", { className: "deja-endpoint", role: "status" },
          status === "unknown"
            ? "Checking /api/deja-search …"
            : status === "present"
              ? "dsh-deja " + (version || "(unknown version)") + " is serving the full-text search endpoint."

        status === "absent"
          ? h("div", { className: "deja-setting deja-keybinding" },
            h("code", { className: "deja-install-command" }, INSTALL_COMMAND),
            h("button", { type: "button", onClick: async () => setCopied(await copyText(INSTALL_COMMAND)) },
              copied ? "Copied" : "Copy install command"),
            h("span", { className: "deja-setting-hint" }, "Replace web with your profile name (for example desktop), then reload this page after installing."),
          )
          : null,

    }

    function Settings({ prefs, shortcuts, route }) {
      const value = usePreferences(prefs);
      // Only a confirmed, working route may offer sidebar features. "unknown"
      // is the probe in flight, so it is not usable either — this matches
      // Sidebar's `status === "present"` gate and avoids showing switches that
      // do nothing for a moment. The composer draft needs no route and stays.
      const status = useSearchRoute(route || searchRoute());
      const sidebarUsable = status === "present";

        h("span", null, h("strong", null, title), h("span", { className: "deja-setting-hint" }, hint)),

        h("h2", null, "Deja"),
        h("p", null, "Search your conversation history with the local Deja index."),
        // Two workflow groups, as dsh-shortcuts groups its commands: the
        // composer draft stands alone, and the two sidebar features share the
        // full-text-search heading so the docs' "two sections" is what renders.
        h("h3", null, "In-conversation search"),
        toggle("conversation", "Search this conversation", "Fill the message input with a search command for the current session. Existing draft text becomes the query; nothing is sent automatically. Customize the key below."),
        ...(sidebarUsable ? [
          h("h3", { key: "fulltext-heading" }, "Deja full-text search"),
          toggle("sidebar", "Deja search in the sidebar", "Open sidebar search, then click its magnifying glass again to search DSH conversation text with Deja. Click again to return to the regular results."),
          toggle("opensDeja", "Deja cross-session shortcut", "Enable the shortcut that opens Deja full-text search for DSH conversations. Customize its key below. The magnifying glass returns the native search."),
        ] : []),
        h(EndpointStatus, { route: route || searchRoute() }),
        h("h3", null, "Customize shortcuts"),
        h("p", { className: "deja-setting-hint" }, "Click Change shortcut, press the combination you want, then release to save. These stay in sync with DSH's built-in shortcut editor."),
        shortcuts?.edit && shortcuts?.recording && shortcuts?.catalog && shortcuts?.config
          ? h(React.Fragment, null,
            h(ShortcutBinding, { shortcuts, id: "deja.search-session", title: "Search this conversation" }),
            ...(sidebarUsable ? [
              h(ShortcutBinding, { key: "deja.search-sessions", shortcuts, id: "deja.search-sessions", title: "Deja cross-session search" }),
              h(ShortcutBinding, { key: "session.search", shortcuts, id: "session.search", title: "Open sidebar search" }),
            ] : []),
          )
          : h("p", null, "This DSH version has no shortcut editing service. Upgrade DSH to change these bindings."),
      );
    }

    // DSH exposes an addressable slot anchor but no sidebar-search provider
    // extension. Keep this adapter inside that anchor, use semantic controls,
    // and stand down if its shape is unavailable. Never replace slot owners or
    // reach into React internals. Removing the adapter restores native content.
    function attachSidebar(anchor, prefs, changed) {
      const input = anchor.querySelector('input[type="text"]');
      const button = input?.parentElement?.querySelector('button[aria-expanded]');
      const list = anchor.querySelector('[class*="_listArea"]');
      if (!input || !button || !list) return null;
      const target = document.createElement("div");
      target.className = "deja-sidebar-results";
      target.dataset.dejaResults = "";
      target.hidden = true;
      list.parentElement.appendChild(target);
      const old = { hidden: list.hidden, title: button.getAttribute("title"), pressed: button.getAttribute("aria-pressed") };
      let active = false;
      const publish = () => changed({ active, query: input.value, target });
      const setActive = (next) => {
        active = next;
        list.hidden = active || old.hidden;
        target.hidden = !active;
        button.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(active));
        button.setAttribute("title", active ? "Deja search — click for regular search" : "Search conversation text with Deja");
        publish();
      };
      // The native search is reachable whenever its list is the one showing.
      publish();
      const click = (event) => {
        if (button.getAttribute("aria-expanded") !== "true") return;
        event.preventDefault();
        event.stopPropagation();
        // The magnifier is the escape hatch back to DSH's title search.
        prefs.releaseOpen();
        setActive(!active);
        input.focus();
      };
      const update = () => { if (active) publish(); };
      const sync = () => { if (active && button.getAttribute("aria-expanded") !== "true") setActive(false); };
      // A search opened by the Mod+Shift+K gesture becomes Deja's when the
      // switch is on: that expansion lands in full-text mode. Native Mod+K
      // still opens DSH's regular title search. The sidebar's own re-render
      // races the shortcut, so poll briefly and give up cleanly — an
      // unclaimed opening keeps the native search.
      const claimOpen = () => {

// indexes it by the uuid, so that is the id every hook is given.
function bareSessionId(id) {
  return String(id || "").replace(/^session-/, "");
}

function sessionId(agent) {
  return bareSessionId((agent && (agent.sessionId || (agent.session && agent.session.id))) || "");
}

// The workspace a session belongs to. One web or tui process serves sessions
// from every workspace and never changes directory, so process.cwd() is only
// where dsh was launched; the session header carries the directory the session
// was opened in.
function sessionCwd(agent) {
  const header = agent && agent.session && agent.session.header;
  return (header && header.cwd) || process.cwd();
}

// askHook runs a hook once for both readers. Where a page will show the
// person's lines, deja is asked for its JSON reply: additionalContext, the
// text --plain prints, goes to the model and systemMessage waits on the board.
// Anywhere else — tui, headless, sdk — it stays --plain. deja marks a note
// shown when it prints it, so asking for notes nobody will read spends them,
// and `/deja` and the next Claude Code session would not see them either.
function askHook(plain, json, payload, sid, board) {
  if (!board.hasReader()) return run(plain, payload);
  const reply = splitHookReply(run(json, payload));
  board.push(sid, reply.notes);
  return reply.context;
}

function autoRecall(ctx, board) {
  let asked = "";
  let askedIn = "";
  let askedBy = "";
  let recalled = "";
  const compacted = new Set();
  watchCompaction(ctx, compacted);

  guarded(() =>
    ctx.systemPrompt.context({
      name: "deja:recall",
      order: 120,
      interpolate: false,
      text: (assembly) => {
        const agent = assembly && assembly.agent;
        if (!agent) return "";
        const prompt = lastHumanText(agent);
        if (!prompt) return "";
        const cwd = sessionCwd(agent);
        const sid = sessionId(agent);
        const afterCompaction = compacted.delete(sid);
        // The same question asked in another workspace is a different question,
        // and so is one asked again after its session compacted: deja then
        // answers with the recovery packet, which only a prompt naming the
        // session gets back.
        if (prompt !== asked || cwd !== askedIn || sid !== askedBy || afterCompaction) {
          asked = prompt;
          askedIn = cwd;
          askedBy = sid;
          recalled = inert(askHook(
            ["hook-prompt", "--plain"],
            ["hook-prompt"],
            JSON.stringify({ prompt, cwd, session_id: sid }),
            sid,
            board,
          ));
        }
        // Silence is the common case: this speaks only when the history answers.
        return recalled;
      },
    }),
  );
}

// The person's half. dsh shows nobody what a plugin hands the model, and has
// no notice channel a host plugin can write to, so deja's lines wait on a board
// and the browser half (client.js) asks for them under the composer. The route
// rides dsh's own /api mount, which applies the same Host/Origin fence and
// browser login as every other call the page makes. Only a profile that serves
// that page — the connection service and a web server both — registers it;
// headless, tui, sdk and an older dsh never do, and keep asking deja for
// --plain. A second copy of the plugin finds the path taken and stands down.
const NOTES_PATH = "/api/deja-notes";

function notesRoute(ctx, board) {
  if (typeof ctx.inject !== "function") return;
  try {
    ctx.inject(["connection", "webServer"], (c) => {
      const registered = guarded(() =>
        c.connection.fetch.register({
          path: NOTES_PATH,
          methods: ["GET"],
          requestBody: "buffered",
          fetch: async (request) => {
            let sid = "";
            try {
              sid = bareSessionId(new URL(request.url).searchParams.get("session"));
            } catch {}
            return Response.json({ notes: sid ? board.take(sid) : [] }, { headers: { "cache-control": "no-store" } });
          },
        }),
      );
      if (registered) board.setReader();
    });
  } catch {}
}

// runAsync is run for a seam dsh awaits, so the event loop goes on while deja
// answers. It never rejects.
function runAsync(args, input) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    try {
      const child = execFile(DEJA, args, { windowsHide: true, encoding: "utf8", timeout: 20000, maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }, (err, stdout) =>
        resolve(err ? "" : String(stdout || "").trim()),
      );
      child.on("error", () => resolve(""));
      child.stdin.on("error", () => {});
      child.stdin.end(input);
    } catch {
      resolve("");
    }
  });
}

// Compaction shadows the turns it summarises but leaves them in the session
// log, so deja reads the session there as compaction/start lands and keeps a
// recovery packet: the task, each command with how it went, what was still
// open. The log is written behind the session, so it is flushed first. dsh
// assembles a step's context before its agent/pre-step waterfall, where the
// compaction runs, so the step that compacts waits there for the capture and
// the packet rides the recall of the next step, or of the next turn.
function watchCompaction(ctx, compacted) {
  if (typeof ctx.on !== "function") return;
  const capturing = new Map();
  const listen = (c) =>
    c.on("session/event", (session, event) => {
      if (!session || !event || event.type !== "compaction/start") return;
      const sid = bareSessionId(session.id || (session.header && session.header.id));
      if (!sid) return;
      const cwd = (session.header && session.header.cwd) || process.cwd();
      // One compaction can follow another inside a step; two captures at once
      // contend for the index and the loser marks the packet unavailable, so
      // each waits for the one before it.
      const before = capturing.get(sid) || Promise.resolve();
      const capture = before.then(async () => {
        try {
          if (c.sessions && typeof c.sessions.flush === "function") await c.sessions.flush(session);
        } catch {}
        await runAsync(["hook-precompact"], JSON.stringify({ session_id: sid, cwd, harness: "deepseek" }));
        compacted.add(sid);
      });
      capturing.set(sid, capture);
      capture.then(() => {
        if (capturing.get(sid) === capture) capturing.delete(sid);
      });
    });
  try {
    if (typeof ctx.inject === "function") ctx.inject(["sessions"], listen);
    else listen(ctx);
  } catch {}
  try {
    ctx.on("agent/pre-step", async (step, next) => {
      const sid = sessionId(step && step.agent);
      if (capturing.has(sid)) await capturing.get(sid);
      const decision = await next();
      if (capturing.has(sid)) await capturing.get(sid);
      return decision;
    });
  } catch {}
}

// The point of action, as `deja install dsh-auto` wires it. tools/post-execute
// runs on every tool result, and an accept decision's additionalContexts reach
// the model on the next step: a read, edit or write gets what deja knows about
// the file, a bash that exited non-zero gets the fix this machine found for
// that error before. The before-seam, tools/execute, has no channel to the
// model.
function toolNotes(ctx) {
  if (typeof ctx.on !== "function") return;
  try {
    ctx.on("tools/post-execute", async (exec, result, next) => {
      const decision = await next();
      try {
        if (!decision || decision.kind !== "accept" || !exec) return decision;
        const note = await toolNote(exec, result);
        if (!note) return decision;
        return {
          ...decision,
          additionalContexts: [...(decision.additionalContexts || []), noteMessage(note)],
        };
      } catch {
        return decision;
      }
    });
  } catch {}
}

// A session is over when dsh disposes of it, or when the process goes: on
// 0.1.1-rc.2 the headless profile exits without disposing anything, and only
// process "exit" runs. The digest and the recall stamp a session live, which
// keeps it out of its own MCP recall; dropping the stamp lets the next session
// be answered with it now rather than twenty minutes from now.
function sessionEnds(ctx) {
  if (typeof ctx.on !== "function") return;
  // Each live session with the directory it opened in: the end refreshes that
  // project's start digest, so the next session there sees this one.
  const live = new Map();
  const end = (sid) => {
    if (!sid || !live.has(sid)) return;
    const cwd = live.get(sid);
    live.delete(sid);
    run(["hook-session-end"], JSON.stringify({ session_id: sid, cwd }));
  };
  try {
    ctx.on("session/created", (session) => {
      const sid = bareSessionId(session && session.id);
      if (sid) live.set(sid, (session.header && session.header.cwd) || process.cwd());
    });
    ctx.on("session/disposed", (session) => end(bareSessionId(session && session.id)));
    process.on("exit", () => {
      for (const sid of [...live.keys()]) end(sid);
    });
  } catch {}
}

async function toolNote(exec, result) {
  const args = exec.arguments || {};
  const base = { session_id: sessionId(exec.agent), cwd: sessionCwd(exec.agent) };
  const editFields = {};
  if (args.old_string || args.old_str) editFields.old_string = String(args.old_string || args.old_str);
  if (args.new_string || args.new_str || args.content || args.file_text) editFields.new_string = String(args.new_string || args.new_str || args.content || args.file_text);
  if ((exec.name === "read" || exec.name === "edit" || exec.name === "write") && args.file_path) {
    return runAsync(["hook-tool", "--plain"], JSON.stringify({
      tool_name: exec.name,
      tool_input: { file_path: String(args.file_path), ...editFields },
      ...base,
    }));
  }
  // The profile's other editor names the file "path"; view is its read.
  if (exec.name === "str_replace_editor" && args.path) {
    return runAsync(["hook-tool", "--plain"], JSON.stringify({
      tool_name: args.command === "view" ? "read" : "edit",
      tool_input: { file_path: String(args.path), ...editFields },
      ...base,
    }));
  }
  // pwsh is the Windows shell, with the same markers.
  if (exec.name === "bash" || exec.name === "pwsh") {
    const status = exitStatus(resultText(result));
    if (!(result && result.isError) && !status.failed) return "";
    return runAsync(["hook-tool-after", "--plain"], JSON.stringify({
      tool_name: exec.name === "pwsh" ? "powershell" : "bash",
      tool_input: { command: String(args.command || "") },
      tool_response: status.body,
      ...base,
    }));
  }
  return "";
}

// A context message the way dsh's own plugins build one: user role, a
// producer-owned source so it is not read back as something the person typed,
// a fresh id, frozen. v4 session format refuses the bare "plugin" kind, so the
// producer owns "plugin:deja" — the value dsh's own v3→v4 migration assigns an
// unmapped plugin.
function noteMessage(text) {
  const message = {
    role: "user",
    content: [{ type: "text", text }],
    source: { kind: "plugin:deja", form: "notice" },
    id: randomUUID(),
  };
  Object.freeze(message.content[0]);
  Object.freeze(message.content);
  Object.freeze(message.source);
  return Object.freeze(message);
}

// lastHumanText is the newest thing the person actually typed. At assembly
// time the message has already left the inbox and has not been appended as a
// "user/message" yet — the only durable record of it is the inbox splice that
// carried it in, so both are read. Anything a plugin contributed is skipped:
// those carry a source of their own.
function lastHumanText(agent) {
  for (const event of newestEvents(agent && agent.session)) {
    if (!event) continue;
    if (event.type === "user/message" && isHuman(event.data)) return userText(event.data);
    if (event.type === "agent/inbox/spliced") {
      const inserted = event.data && event.data.inserted;
      if (!Array.isArray(inserted)) continue;
      for (let j = inserted.length - 1; j >= 0; j--) {
        if (isHuman(inserted[j])) return userText(inserted[j]);
      }
    }
  }
  return "";
}

function isHuman(message) {
  return Boolean(message) && (!message.source || message.source.kind === "user");
}

// `deja install dsh` writes plugins of its own into DSH_HOME and adds them to
// the profile, so a user who ran the installer and then added this package has
// both: two `/deja` commands, the same recall on the system prompt twice, and
// deja's MCP server answering the same six questions the tools here do. What
// the installer wrote wins — it is the copy `deja install` keeps current — and
// this package contributes only the parts that are missing.
//
// The two halves are separate on purpose: `deja install dsh` writes command.js
// and the MCP row, and only `deja install dsh-auto` adds auto.js. A profile can
// have the command from the installer and still want recall from here.
function cliPluginDir() {
  const home = process.env.DSH_HOME || join(homedir(), ".dsh");
  return join(home, "plugins", "deja");
}

function installedByCLI(file) {
  try {
    return existsSync(join(cliPluginDir(), file));
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function apply(ctx, config) {
  const adds = contributions(
    { command: installedByCLI("command.js"), auto: installedByCLI("auto.js") },
    config,
  );
  const board = noteBoard();
  // User-initiated search remains available when automatic recall is disabled.
  installSearchRoute(ctx, DEJA);
  if (adds.tools) tools(ctx);
  if (adds.command) command(ctx, board);
  if (adds.recall) {
    autoDigest(ctx, board);
    autoRecall(ctx, board);
    notesRoute(ctx, board);
    toolNotes(ctx);
    sessionEnds(ctx);
  }
}

apply.inject = ["tools", "commands", "systemPrompt"];

export default apply;

export const SEARCH_PATH = "/api/deja-search";
export const SEARCH_LIMIT = 20;
export const SEARCH_TIMEOUT = 20000;
export const SEARCH_MAX_BUFFER = 2 * 1024 * 1024;

// Keep the entire query one argv entry, including command names and flags.
export function searchArgv(query) {
  return ["search", "--harness", "deepseek", "--json", "--limit", String(SEARCH_LIMIT), "--", query];
}

// A callback seam lets tests exercise the actual process options without
// starting a shell, touching an index, or reading anybody's session history.
export function createSearchExecutor(execute = execFile) {
  return (binary, args, signal) => new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    try {
      execute(binary, args, {
        shell: false,
        windowsHide: true,
        encoding: "utf8",
        timeout: SEARCH_TIMEOUT,
        maxBuffer: SEARCH_MAX_BUFFER,

const text = (value) => typeof value === "string" ? value : "";
const number = (value) => typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : 0;

export function normalizeSearchResult(payload) {
  // Older deja releases emitted a bare array for exact matches.
  const rows = Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : payload?.hits;
  // Go encodes a nil hit slice as null when there are no matches.
  if (!Array.isArray(rows) && !(rows === null && payload && !Array.isArray(payload))) {
    throw new Error("invalid search envelope");
  }
  const hits = [];
  for (const row of rows || []) {
    const session = row?.session;
    if (session?.harness !== "deepseek" || !text(session.id)) continue;
    const bare = session.id.replace(/^session-/, "");
    if (!bare) continue;
    hits.push({
      sessionId: `session-${bare}`,
      title: text(session.title),
      project: text(session.project),
      updated: text(session.updated),
      snippets: Array.isArray(row.snippets) ? row.snippets.filter((s) => typeof s === "string").slice(0, 3) : [],
      count: number(row.count),
      score: number(row.score),
    });
  }
  const total = Array.isArray(payload) ? rows.length : Math.max(0, number(payload.total));

    hits: hits.slice(0, SEARCH_LIMIT),
    hasMore: payload.capped === true || total > (rows || []).length || hits.length > SEARCH_LIMIT,
    total,

function json(body, status = 200) {
  return Response.json(body, { status, headers: { "cache-control": "no-store" } });
}

function failure(status, code, message) {
  return json({ hits: [], hasMore: false, error: { code, message } }, status);
}

function executionFailure(error) {
  if (error?.code === "ENOENT") return failure(503, "unavailable", "Deja is not installed or could not be found.");
  if (error?.code === "ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER") return failure(502, "output_limit", "Deja search exceeded the output limit.");
  if (error?.killed || error?.code === "ETIMEDOUT") return failure(504, "timeout", "Deja search timed out.");
  return failure(502, "search_failed", "Deja search failed. Check the local Deja installation and index.");
}

export function createSearchHandler(binary, { run = createSearchExecutor() } = {}) {
  return async (request) => {
    if (request.method !== "GET") return failure(405, "method_not_allowed", "Use GET for search.");
    let query;
    let url;
    try {
      url = new URL(request.url);
      query = (url.searchParams.get("q") || "").trim();
    } catch {
      return failure(400, "invalid_request", "Invalid search URL.");
    }
    // The probe answers before any deja work: the browser only needs to know
    // whether this route exists and which plugin serves it.
    if (url.searchParams.has("probe")) {
      return json({ ok: true, plugin: "dsh-deja", version: VERSION });
    }
    if (!query) return json({ hits: [], hasMore: false, total: 0, tier: "" });
    if (query.length > 500) return failure(400, "query_too_long", "Search queries must be at most 500 characters.");
    const cancelled = () => failure(499, "cancelled", "Deja search was cancelled.");
    if (request.signal?.aborted) return cancelled();
    if (!binary) return failure(503, "unavailable", "Deja is not installed or could not be found.");

    try {
      stdout = await run(binary, searchArgv(query), request.signal);
    } catch (error) {
      return request.signal?.aborted ? cancelled() : executionFailure(error);
    }
    if (request.signal?.aborted) return cancelled();
    try {
      return json(normalizeSearchResult(JSON.parse(stdout)));
    } catch {
      return failure(502, "invalid_output", "Deja returned invalid search data. Update Deja and try again.");
    }
  };
}

// Match notesRoute: DSH's API mount supplies its Host/Origin and login fence.
// Cordis owns route disposal; duplicate/older/headless hosts may stand down.

          path: SEARCH_PATH,
          methods: ["GET"],
          requestBody: "buffered",
          fetch: createSearchHandler(binary, options),
        });
      } catch {}
    });
  } catch {}
}
